medium:
Use case: stylized-concept. Edit the supplied native game character design into a clean production MODEL TURNAROUND sheet for SternenBuergerchen. Image 1 is the ACTUAL EXISTING KENNEY-BASED GAME MODEL: it is the mandatory body/proportions/style reference, not an illustration to beautify into a realistic soldier. Its left character is the unarmored starting body; the other two are rough armor prototypes, not finished designs. KEEP the same huge Kenney head, small simplified hands, short stylized body/limbs, existing face and clean low-poly mesh look. The precise existing body proportions override the human anatomy of the Star Citizen reference. The armor must fit the existing rig, not redesign the person. Image 2 supplies only the requested armor construction and recognizable silhouette. No existing accessory helmet geometry needs to be copied. Present ONE coherent outfit, repeated identically in FOUR clear orthographic panels: FRONT, BACK, SIDE, TOP. Front/back/side show the whole figure, same scale, neutral relaxed A-pose, fingers simple. TOP is an actual overhead orthographic camera looking down on the same helmet, collar, shoulders and body, not an extra face portrait. No weapons, no stands, no scenery, no floating gear. Plain light warm-grey background, soft neutral studio light, orthographic technical presentation. Consistency is crucial: identical chest shape, shoulder plates, helmet, joints, materials and details in every view. Labels only: VORNE, HINTEN, SEITE, OBEN. Readable simplified construction with beveled polygonal volumes, dark flexible joint gaps, restrained trim. Avoid realism, normal-sized adult heads, gritty photographic textures, over-detailed micro-greebles, flat plates that look pasted on, excessive body enlargement, a generic smooth bucket helmet, or a whole new art style. This is a 2D design reference, not a screenshot of an implemented model.
OUTFIT: MITTLERE RÜSTUNG inspired by Star Citizen ORC-mkV shown in Image 2. Slim agile combat shell: distinctive two angular pectoral plates integrated into the vest, three articulated abdominal plates, small faceted shoulder caps, forearm guards, modest thigh/knee/shin protection, dark flexible undersuit clearly showing between hard parts. Own angular open-face helmet frame with shaped brow/temples/chin protection; original Kenney face visible. No high padded heavy collar. Neutral warm light-grey/sand ceramic, charcoal undersuit, small amber details; do NOT copy the green color of Image 2. Keep moderate readable detail, turn the rough prototype into a coherent wearable suit. Medium must remain visibly slimmer than a Morozov heavy outfit, especially at shoulders, waist and legs.
